purpose: Interval between the last hike of each tightening cycle and the equity bottom, from first-hand data. One-off research output; NOT part of the daily pipeline.

definitions.tightening_cycle: a maximal run of consecutive increases in the spliced policy rate. A cut ends the cycle; a hold does not interrupt it.
definitions.last_hike: the final increase before the first subsequent cut
definitions.equity_bottom: lowest close inside [last hike -24m, last hike +36m]
definitions.drawdown: bottom close vs the highest close in the 252 trading days strictly BEFORE the window opens
definitions.interval_months: bottom date - last hike date, in days / (365.25/12)
definitions.supplementary_local_bottom: lowest close within +/-6 months of the last hike. Reported because the memory table's claim is about a bottom NEAR the last hike, which the five-year window minimum does not measure.
definitions.supplementary_is_window_edge_artifact: true when the window minimum sits within 10 trading days of the window opening, i.e. the index only rose inside the window and the 'bottom' is the left edge rather than a trough.

synthetic_cases.note: These drive find_cycles() directly, so a FAIL is a bug in the cycle definition. Run `python3 rate_cycles_v1.py --selftest`. Deliberately not wired into run_daily.sh or the daily validators.

cases.rule: 连加 3 次后持平，再降息 → 最后一次加息 = 第 3 次加息，持平不中断周期
连加 2 次、持平、再加 1 次、然后降息 → 最后一次加息 = 第 3 次，仍是同一个周期
只加不降 → ongoing，没有『最后一次加息』，last_hike 只是目前最近一次

after.meaning: UPPER BOUND of the target range

policy_rate_splice.note: The two series measure different things, so the splice prints a level break. It is a downward step and therefore cannot create a false hike; it also falls inside the 2007-08 easing.

limitations: FRED DFEDTAR is a compiled series: before 1994 the FOMC did not announce its target in real time, so pre-1994 'hike dates' are after-the-fact reconstructions of a target that markets had to infer at the time.
DFEDTARU is the UPPER BOUND of a target range, not a point target; it is not the same quantity as DFEDTAR and the two are never averaged here.
^NDX begins 1985-10-01, so cycles before that have no NDX column.
ICE BofA HY OAS is unavailable before 2023-11 (rolling FRED window, no ALFRED vintages), so it is null for every completed cycle here.
Index closes are unadjusted (auto_adjust=False); index levels carry no dividends, so this is a price-return view.

The specified drawdown anchors its reference peak in the 252 trading days before the window OPENS, i.e. ~24 months before the last hike. Over a 60-month window that anchor can be far from the peak the bottom actually fell from, so a severe bottom can score a small drawdown (2015-18: bottoms at the COVID crash, scores -1.51%). The supplementary running-peak drawdown is reported alongside it.
In a cycle where the index only rose inside the window, the window minimum IS the left edge and is not a bottom in any economic sense. Those rows are flagged supplementary_is_window_edge_artifact.
An ongoing cycle has no last hike. Its intervals are provisional and its window runs past the data, so it is marked incomplete and no bottom is concluded.
